sehemu: Part III: Procedure, Powers and Privileges of Parliament
maudhui: (1) After a General Election the President shall summon a meeting of the new Parliament to take place before the expiration of seven days following the declaration of the results of the General Election in all constituencies, except constituencies where the election has been cancelled and is to be held afresh. (2) The President shall not have power to dissolve Parliament at any time except - (a) if Parliament has completed its term under Article 65, or at any time during the last twelve months of its life, except where the Speaker has received a formal notice proposing the establishment of a Special Committee of Inquiry for the purpose of removing the President from office under Article 46A; (b) if Parliament refuses to approve the budget proposed by the Government; (c) if Parliament refuses to pass a Bill in accordance with Article 97(4); (d) if Parliament refuses to pass a motion fundamental to Government policy and the President considers that the proper course is not to appoint another Prime Minister but to call a General Election; or (e) where, because of the proportion of representation of political parties in Parliament, the President considers that the existing Government has no legitimacy to continue and it is not possible to form a new Government. (3) Upon expiry of the life of Parliament, Parliament shall be deemed dissolved; provided that where such period expires while the United Republic is at war, Parliament may from time to time extend the period specified in Article 65 for periods not exceeding twelve months at a time, but the life of Parliament shall not be extended under this subarticle for more than five years. (4) Where a state of emergency arises, or where there exists an emergency which in the opinion of the President requires the summoning of Parliament, and Parliament has been dissolved and the results of the majority of votes in the General Election have not been declared, the President may by special proclamation summon a meeting of Parliament and direct the Speaker and all persons who were Members immediately before dissolution to attend that meeting.

(2) The President shall not have power to dissolve Parliament at any time except - (a) if Parliament has completed its term under Article 65, or at any time during the last twelve months of its life, except where the Speaker has received a formal notice proposing the establishment of a Special Committee of Inquiry for the purpose of removing the President from office under Article 46A; (b) if Parliament refuses to approve the budget proposed by the Government; (c) if Parliament refuses to pass a Bill in accordance with Article 97(4); (d) if Parliament refuses to pass a motion fundamental to Government policy and the President considers that the proper course is not to appoint another Prime Minister but to call a General Election; or (e) where, because of the proportion of representation of political parties in Parliament, the President considers that the existing Government has no legitimacy to continue and it is not possible to form a new Government.

(3) Upon expiry of the life of Parliament, Parliament shall be deemed dissolved; provided that where such period expires while the United Republic is at war, Parliament may from time to time extend the period specified in Article 65 for periods not exceeding twelve months at a time, but the life of Parliament shall not be extended under this subarticle for more than five years.

(4) Where a state of emergency arises, or where there exists an emergency which in the opinion of the President requires the summoning of Parliament, and Parliament has been dissolved and the results of the majority of votes in the General Election have not been declared, the President may by special proclamation summon a meeting of Parliament and direct the Speaker and all persons who were Members immediately before dissolution to attend that meeting.
